definition: Content-addressed identity anchor — SHA-256 over a sorted list of (field, normalized_value) pairs from a schema's ess_fields. Two records with the same ESS digest are the same entity by construction (T1 match). NOT the same as EntitySense (spiritwriter/fabric/shard.py), the CMC homonym sense-disambiguator on a ShardAtom — different concept, dangerously similar name; do not conflate.
SQLite-backed runtime engine for definition-based entity resolution. Domain-agnostic — supply a CanonicalSchema describing how your entities are identified.

spiritwriter-core's definition-based entity resolution system — the resolver only. CanonicalRegistry is its runtime engine. Renamed from 'shingles' (overlapping shields metaphor > overlapping roof tiles; avoids medical connotation). Does NOT encompass shingled extraction; that's a separate primitive (see docs/shingled-extraction.md). Reserved for deep-dive technical docs (e.g. docs/entity-resolution.md body); do not use on marketing surfaces (root README, getting-started, landing pages).

Atom extraction primitive — turn long-form text into ShardAtoms via overlapping windows + multi-pass consensus voting; only atoms that appear across multiple passes survive. Separate from Phalanx (the resolver); together they form the extract → resolve loop. 'Shingled' is the process adjective (overlapping coverage like roofing shingles); the historical noun 'shingles' is retired.
Pragmatic implementation of Consensus Memory Canonicalization using ESS + tiered resolution + overlapping-window extraction. Zero new dependencies (no vec0, no LLM clustering).

sqlite-vec's virtual-table extension for vector search inside SQLite. Status in spiritwriter-core: NOT a current dependency. Listed in spiritwriter-canonicalize.md as an optional future path for T3/T4 embedding-backed fuzzy matching once string similarity stops being enough. The historical docs/specs/cmc-lite-v0.1.md spec planned to use vec0; the shipped CanonicalRegistry deliberately doesn't (see that spec's status header).

Full canonicalization pipeline drawing on academic prior art (EDC/EMNLP 2024, Graphiti/Zep, SimpleMem). Four stages: Normalize & Embed, Cluster & Block, Consensus & Merge, Reify & Store. Targets ≥85% recall on semantic duplicates with ≤5% false-merge rate.
Content-addressed bundle of knowledge atoms. shard_id = SHA-256 of canonical JSON of {atoms, scope, origin}.

Single knowledge unit inside a MemoryShard — a distilled fact/decision/convention for prompt hydration. Has text, kind (an AtomKind), optional entity/key/value/confidence/source_ref, plus optional CMC enrichment key_definition + sense (an EntitySense). DISTINCT from DocumentAtom: a ShardAtom is knowledge, a DocumentAtom is document structure. They are different models in different files and do not share fields.

Enum of the KIND of knowledge a ShardAtom carries: fact | decision | convention | preference | entity | context | checkpoint | instruction. DISTINCT from AtomType, which classifies a DocumentAtom by document-layout role. 'kind' = what the knowledge is, not a layout role.

Smallest unit of extracted document STRUCTURE produced by DocumentIngestor (rich PDF analysis): content + page/bbox location + topics/entities + importance + caption/figure metadata, typed by AtomType. DISTINCT from ShardAtom — a DocumentAtom represents a chunk of a document's layout; a ShardAtom is distilled knowledge. A DocumentAtom has no key/value/sense and is never aligned into a MemoryShard directly.

Enum of a DocumentAtom's document-layout ROLE: title | abstract | section_header | paragraph | quote | citation | figure | chart | table | equation | diagram | author | date | keyword. DISTINCT from AtomKind, which classifies a ShardAtom by knowledge kind. 'type' = layout role, not a knowledge kind.

Optional sense disambiguator on a ShardAtom's entity (the CMC 'Bear Problem', cmc-spec-v0.1.md §5.5): sense_type | scoped_to | domain | gloss | context. Powers the familiarize alignment sense-gate — keeps homonyms apart (Bear the dog vs bear the animal) before any LLM adjudication. DISTINCT from Entity Sense Signature (ESS), the Phalanx content-addressed identity anchor over ess_fields — different concept, dangerously similar name; do not conflate.

Optional ShardAtom field — a one-sentence natural-language definition of the atom's key (the EDC 'Define' step from CMC). Lets familiarize alignment match concepts by meaning (database approx datastore) instead of by key spelling. Excluded from the atom's content_hash.

Writes hash-chained JSONL event logs — tamper-evident audit trail. Each event SHA-256s its own payload and links to the previous event's hash. Mutate any event after the fact, verify_chain() returns False.
Pure function on a list of event dicts. Checks event hash, prev_event_hash linkage, first-event invariant. Cannot detect tail-truncation.

Typed, signed token authorizing the holder to act within a defined attenuation. Capabilities form chains via parent_cap_id; leaf authority is the intersection of every caveat in the chain. A capability is NOT a shard — distinct primitive.
Ordered list of capability IDs from root to leaf. Used in TraceEmitter event context and provenance queries (events_under_chain).
Restriction on a capability. Closed set of three types: expires_at, scope_limit, max_delegation_depth. Verifiers MUST fail closed on unknown types.
Memory shard field with five values: permanent | stable | active | session | checkpoint. Influences retention behavior.
AES-256-GCM symmetric encryption envelope for a MemoryShard. Operator and key-holder cooperate. Fields: shard_id, scope, encrypted_payload, nonce, atom_count, created_at, origin_agent, content_hash.

NaCl sealed-box (Curve25519 + XSalsa20-Poly1305) envelope for a MemoryShard. Operator never sees plaintext. Fields: shard_id, scope, sealed_payload, owner_pubkey, atom_count, created_at, origin_agent, content_hash.
Bearer credential packaging decryption keys + scopes + capabilities + budget for sub-agent delegation. Sub-agents present the token; the store validates and decrypts only what's entitled.
Confidence tier for entity resolution. T1_EXACT (0.95) | T2_STRONG (0.85) | T3_FUZZY (0.70) | T4_WEAK (0.50) | NO_MATCH (0.0). T1+T2 auto-merge; T3+T4 flag-only.

Self-hashing JSON document binding APK SHA-256 + every extracted file's hash + every finding's derivation event + final report hash. witness_sha256 is computed over the document with that field nulled.
Binary extractor from the Rizin reverse-engineering framework. Used by spiritwriter.audit to extract strings, imports, exports from DEX and .so files. Tested with rz-bin 0.8.2.
The content-addressed memory + capability wire format. Documented in docs/substrate-flavor.md. Library-free agents can produce/verify shards with just sha256 + Ed25519 + canonical JSON.
Capability revocation lists. Explicitly listed as future work in docs/substrate-flavor.md — NOT currently implemented. Do not claim this exists.
Time-bounded trust periods. Explicitly listed as future work in docs/substrate-flavor.md — NOT currently implemented. Do not claim this exists.
HTTP protocol for shard distribution. Explicitly listed as future work in docs/substrate-flavor.md — NOT currently implemented. Do not claim this exists.

Acronym hallucinated by Claude Chat for what is actually documented as 'Spiritwriter Substrate' in docs/substrate-flavor.md. No SW-CAP spec exists. Use 'Spiritwriter Substrate' or 'capability' instead.

Phrase hallucinated by Claude Chat. Capabilities and shards are DISTINCT primitives — a shard cites cap_id but the cap exists independently. Use 'capability' or 'cap' for the cap, 'MemoryShard' for the shard.
Phrase hallucinated by Claude Chat. 'Bootstrap' refers to giving an agent (this doc + trust roots + delegation bundle) — not a shard. See docs/substrate-flavor.md §5.
Phrase hallucinated by Claude Chat. The mechanism is plain NaCl sealed-box (Curve25519 + XSalsa20-Poly1305) — one ephemeral sender key + one owner keypair. Don't relabel it 'dual-key'.

term: INVENTED: OpenTelemetry span attributes for provenance
definition: Hallucinated integration. spiritwriter trace does NOT use OpenTelemetry. Provenance queries are events_by_cap / events_by_role / events_by_signer / events_under_chain over JSONL.
